record.name: Training data pipeline
record.role: Convert a source collection into useful learning examples.
record.description:
A training pipeline may collect, filter, deduplicate, format, tokenize, and batch data. The mixture controls which patterns the optimizer repeatedly encounters. Quality is not a single scalar: correctness, coverage, provenance, licensing, contamination, and representativeness all matter. Training, validation, and benchmark splits need careful separation and overlap checks. More bytes alone do not guarantee better learning; repeated low-value or contaminated examples can waste compute and distort evaluation.

Training examples also have an availability and transformation history. A label may arrive after an input was first observed, and preprocessing fitted on future or held-out cases can leak information across the evaluation boundary. A deployed artifact should retain which split supplied each learned statistic so later predictions can be reproduced without silently refitting on new data.

Advanced lifecycle practice retains source identity, transformation history, tokenizer version and document-family split assignment together. A train/development/final separation is meaningful only if near-identical families do not cross it. The executable symbol corpus records these fields, while its source is original synthetic material rather than a crawl or human conversation. Development answers support iteration; the first final report records the evaluated checkpoint and cannot be silently rewritten after another update.

The corpus lineage experience now executes a small construction chain: original document families are assigned to splits before normalization; exact training copies can be excluded with retained source pointers; a tokenizer fits only retained training fields; deterministic document sampling and packing produce inspectable arrays.
mechanism: Prepare and document the source mixture.
Filter, deduplicate, tokenize, and form batches.
Track validation and contamination separately from optimization.
Feature construction and normalizer fitting use only the allowed training information.
Evaluation and later monitoring retain their own sample and label-availability boundaries rather than being folded back into the training statistic.
Assign whole document families to splits before tokenization-dependent sampling.
Record final exposure as part of the experimental history, including after importing an older checkpoint.
Compare exact transformed prompt/response pairs, three-word-shingle similarity and known-family relationships without treating any single diagnostic as semantic truth.
Record split seed, transformation, excluded IDs, tokenizer fitting IDs, merge order, sampler cursor and packed indices so the same declared batch can be reconstructed.

science.title: The mixture defines the expected learning signal
science.explanation: Each data source D_j contributes according to its sampling weight w_j. Changing those weights changes which errors the optimizer is asked to reduce most often. Repeating near-duplicates can therefore increase their influence without adding comparable diversity. The same nominal token budget can represent very different learning opportunities.
science.assumptions: This expectation assumes a fixed mixture and loss definition. Curriculum schedules, example weighting, repeated epochs, and adaptive sampling modify the effective weights. Source quality and legal provenance cannot be inferred from the equation.

record.name: Self-attention
record.description:
Self-attention computes content-dependent mixtures of information. Learned projections produce queries, keys, and values. Query–key dot products become scores; scaling, a causal mask when appropriate, and softmax turn them into weights. Those weights mix value vectors. Multiple heads can form different mixtures. A causal decoder prevents a position from using future tokens during training. The atlas displays a small matrix so the relationship between rows, columns, and weighted values remains visible.

Attention learning differentiates both the value path and the probabilities controlling that mixture. A causal mask removes future positions from the allowed softmax support; it is not merely a visual annotation. The executable decoder exposes projected Q/K/V, scores, probabilities and the complete gradient graph. A small analytical example clarifies why changing one score can redistribute weight across all allowed values.

Packing several examples into one input array adds a boundary condition to causal attention. In the corpus experience, a query may use only earlier or current positions from its own sampled document instance within the same block. Adjacent storage does not grant another document access to that context.
mechanism: Project representations into Q, K, and V.
Multiply the weights by V and combine heads.
Form scores only for positions the query may attend to.
Normalize those scores together and mix their value vectors.
Backpropagate through both softmax probabilities and value projections; verify prefix invariance under future-token changes.
Use document-instance IDs as well as causal position order when constructing allowed attention keys.
Keep shifted supervision separate from attention: a next-token label may be just outside the input block without becoming visible input context.

science.title: Scaled dot-product attention
science.equation: A = softmax_rows(QKᵀ / √dₖ + M); Y = AV; Var(qᵀk) ≈ dₖ
science.explanation: Each row of A describes how one query mixes allowed value vectors. Dividing by √dₖ controls score scale: a sum of dₖ independent unit-variance products has variance dₖ. Without that adjustment, larger head widths can push softmax toward saturation. The matrix products expose why data reuse matters on GPU tensor units.
science.assumptions: The variance argument assumes independent, zero-mean, unit-variance query/key coordinates; trained vectors need not satisfy it exactly. M is zero for allowed positions and negative infinity for masked positions. This is one attention head before output projection.

science.title: Trainable attention from Q/K/V through gradients · worked relation
science.explanation: With allowed scores [0,ln3] and scalar values [2,6], attention probabilities are [0.25,0.75] and output is 5. For the output itself as the scalar objective, derivative with respect to score one is 0.25×(2−5)=−0.75 and score two is 0.75×(6−5)=0.75. At the first causal position only value 2 is allowed, so output is 2 regardless of future score or value.
science.assumptions: Scalar value example, softmax over the allowed set, values held fixed for the shown score derivative. Full model also differentiates values and projections.
